improv_extras.concept: drive particle density and color by a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion field so coral/leopard/labyrinth patterns emerge over time

v1.feedback: The Gray-Scott RD genuinely drives the coral ridge topology and the bone/dusty-rose/midnight palette is exactly right — restrained, aged, vitrine-specimen feel. Two concrete improvements: (1) the perfect fibonacci-sphere silhouette reads as 'textured ball' rather than a found coral specimen — break the silhouette with hemisphere clipping or per-lobe radial variation so the outline itself is organic, not geometric; (2) the brief asks for a morph of parent 8ug, not a fresh start — the piece should carry forward 8ug's structural DNA (shell layering, audio-reactive concentric geometry) with RD modulating the surface, rather than building a new form from scratch on a sphere.

v2.feedback: The shell-to-RD chain reads well — 8ug's dome silhouette survives while Gray-Scott ridges add genuine reaction-diffusion texture, not just a rename. Two refinements: the RD UV mapping via aTheta/aPhi will produce a visible seam where theta wraps at 0→2π — consider offsetting the seam to the back of the form or blending it out. Second, without mic input the piece may feel inert since breathing is audio-gated; add a subtle fallback sine-breath (period ~6s, amplitude ~0.08) so the coral pulses even before the user clicks 'grant mic'.
